title: Finite presentations of finitely generated commutative monoids
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative monoid (equivalently, a commutative monoid object in sets with Cartesian product [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]), written additively with identity $0$, and let $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ be a finite generating tuple, allowing $n=0$. Write $\pi:\mathbf N^n\to R$ for the surjective homomorphism $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i r_i$. Then there are finitely many pairs $(a_j,b_j)\in\mathbf N^n\times\mathbf N^n$, $1\leq j\leq m$, with $\pi(a_j)=\pi(b_j)$ such that the relation $\pi(a)=\pi(b)$ is the smallest monoid congruence containing these pairs. Here a monoid congruence is an equivalence relation preserved by addition, and smallest means the intersection of all such congruences containing the pairs. Equivalently, for any commutative monoid $T$ and tuple $t_1,\ldots,t_n\in T$, the assignment $r_i\mapsto t_i$ extends to a unique homomorphism $R\to T$ if and only if $\sum_i (a_j)_i t_i=\sum_i (b_j)_i t_i$ for all $j$. No integrality or saturation hypothesis on $R$ is needed.

mathlib_searches.query: Every finitely generated commutative monoid is finitely presented by finitely many generators and relations.
A finitely generated cancellative commutative monoid has a finite presentation as a quotient of a finite rank free commutative monoid.
